extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funds (IHEs, LEAs, other recipients), Title IX coordinators, school/university administrators, compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for recipients of federal education funds to prevent and respond to sex discrimination in education programs or activities, including recordkeeping, monitoring, facilities, grievance procedures, and scope of protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirement (§106.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.8(f) broadens recordkeeping requirements to apply to all notifications to the Title IX Coordinator about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and all complaints of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many recipients already maintain records under State, local, or prior requirements; for those recipients final §106.8(f) may not impose additional burden. Recipients that only maintained records related to sexual harassment under §106.45(b)(10) (2020 amendments) will face increased burden to preserve records about other forms of sex discrimination. Estimated Year 1 modification burden: LEAs—2 hours each from Title IX Coordinator and administrative assistant; IHEs—4 hours Title IX Coordinator, 8 hours administrative assistant, 4 hours database administrator (at $77.54/hour). Total estimated Year 1 cost ≈ $13,022,034. Ongoing annual increase estimated ≈ $5,237,728. Department received no supplementary data to modify estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor for barriers to reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure their Title IX Coordinator monitors the education program or activity for barriers to reporting conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and take steps reasonably calculated to address such barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not required or prohibited under 2020 amendments, but many recipients (particularly IHEs) already monitor to avoid liability. Low-cost monitoring options include adding questions to existing trainings, roundtables, listening sessions, or conversations with students/employees. Remedial steps are often de minimis (e.g., reminding stakeholders of reporting options, reporting employees who discourage reporting to HR). Wide range of possible responses with varying costs/benefits; Department lacked supplementary data to quantify costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactation space and break time requirements (§106.40(b)(3)(v) & §106.57(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure students and employees can access a lactation space (not a bathroom) that is clean, shielded from view, free from intrusion, and may be used for expressing breast milk or breastfeeding; recipients must provide reasonable break time for employees to express breast milk or breastfeed as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements similar to FLSA and many State laws; Department anticipates de minimis cost because most recipients can repurpose existing space or already comply under FLSA/state/local law/collective bargaining agreements. Temporary or converted spaces are acceptable if available when needed. Added clarification: lactation space must be clean (Department assumes existing cleaning practices make this negligible). Possible management tools: sign-up systems, existing coverage systems for brief breaks, private offices at IHEs. Potential benefits include improved retention of students and employees. Department lacked data to quantify increased demand but expects distributed/de minimis impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications for students because of pregnancy or related conditions (§106.40(b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make reasonable modifications for a student's pregnancy or related conditions (as defined in §106.2) to ensure access to the education program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Builds upon OCR's prior 'reasonable and responsive' standard (2013 Pregnancy Pamphlet). Examples of reasonable adjustments: providing a larger desk, allowing frequent trips to the bathroom, permitting temporary access to elevators. Department expects these requirements to be no more costly than prior OCR interpretations and did not receive data to modify cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation consistent with gender identity (§106.31(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: In limited circumstances where different treatment or separation on the basis of sex is permitted, recipients must not do so in a manner that discriminates on the basis of sex by subjecting a person to more than de minimis harm; policies or practices that prevent participation consistent with gender identity cause more than de minimis harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May require updating policies or training materials but generally will not require construction or new programs. Schools that already permit participation consistent with gender identity may require no changes. Associated costs (training, investigations, potential litigation) are discussed elsewhere in the RIA and are expected to be absorbed into general compliance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of scope of Title IX protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations specify that Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination includes discrimination on the basis of pregnancy or related conditions, sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying scope could increase costs for recipients that have not previously addressed these bases, but Department views the non-monetary benefits (clarity and broader protections) as justifying implementation costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of geographic scope (including off-campus conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Department considered and included additional instances of off-campus conduct within the scope of the final regulations when such conduct occurs under a recipient's education program or activity or contributes to a sex-based hostile environment affecting access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some recipients already address off-campus conduct via alternative disciplinary proceedings; including off-campus conduct may increase recipient costs for investigations and disciplinary actions, but benefits (addressing conduct with profound impacts on students/employees) justify these costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing obligations by educational level
rubrics_metrics.description: Department considered whether regulations should distinguish between educational levels (e.g., LEAs vs IHEs) and enable recipients to adapt fair grievance procedures responsive to their educational environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations allow recipients to adapt procedures to their contexts. Department could not quantify costs/benefits of tailoring but asserts that enabling adaptation supports prompt/effective response to sex discrimination and reduces impediments to Title IX implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply grievance procedures and provide supportive measures and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Final approach applies regulatory grievance procedure requirements to all sex discrimination complaints and requires recipients to provide appropriate supportive measures to complainants and respondents and remedies to any person identified as having equal access limited or denied by sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to safeguard fairness in grievance procedures, protect rights under Title IX, and ensure recipients understand obligations to remedy discrimination. Some associated costs (investigations, appeals, training, remedies) are discussed in the RIA; these costs are part of the Department's determination that the chosen alternative best fulfills Title IX objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish Notice of Nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must publish a notice of nondiscrimination as part of compliance with the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among cost categories in Department accounting (estimated costs provided). Publication is a compliance step to ensure recipients communicate Title IX nondiscrimination obligations to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements and updating training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must train Title IX Coordinators and update training materials to reflect the final regulations and recipients' obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounting table estimates costs for 'Training of Title IX Coordinators' and 'Updating Training Materials.' Training may address scope of protections, reporting/monitoring, supportive measures, grievance procedures, pregnancy/lactation accommodations, and participation consistent with gender identity. Department assumes many recipients will incorporate changes into existing training with limited additional expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation and maintenance of documentation / creation and maintenance of records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must create and maintain documentation related to nondiscrimination policy, grievance procedures, notifications, investigations, supportive measures, and other compliance activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounting table lists 'Creation and Maintenance of Documentation' as a cost category. Department estimated costs for initial and ongoing documentation; many recipients may already have systems in place, but others will incur modification costs (estimates provided elsewhere in the RIA).
